inspection.type:
∀ {k t : ℕ} {C : QuarticQuery.Circuit (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord k t)},
  1 ≤ k →
    1 ≤ t →
      ∀ {n : ℕ} {ε : ℝ},
        0 < ε →
          ε ≤ 1 →
            QuarticQuery.Forrelation.repetitions k (ε / ↑(40 * t)) ≤ n →
              ∀ {x : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.Upper.Loc k t C)} {i : QuarticQuery.Upper.Col t}
                {s : QuarticQuery.Upper.Addr t},
                QuarticQuery.WinsAt (QuarticQuery.P k t) C (2 * t) (40 * t) x i s →
                  ∀ (j : QuarticQuery.Upper.Col t), j ≠ i → 1 - ε ≤ QuarticQuery.Upper.cmpProb n x i j

lean.note: The inequality is pointwise in arbitrary raw x and does not assume anything about the opponent’s promise. Existing source defines cmpProb from the actual comparison algorithm; the chosen n is the paper decoder repetition schedule.

presentation.body: If $i_*$ is a winning column, then for every $j\ne i_*$, its comparison probability satisfies $a_{i_*j}\ge1-\epsilon$. This holds on every input, whether or not the opponent’s partial-function instances are defined.
